title: Texas Longhorns - Wikipedia
content: # Texas Longhorns. Intercollegiate sports teams of the University of Texas at Austin. This article is about the athletics programs of the University of Texas at Austin. | University | University of Texas at Austin |. The **Texas Longhorns** are the athletic teams representing the University of Texas at Austin. Generally, both the men's and women's teams are referred to as the Longhorns, and the mascot is a Texas Longhorn steer named Bevo "Bevo (mascot)"). The University of Texas at Austin is the flagship institution of the University of Texas System. Until Athletic Director Chris Del Conte altered the organizational structure of the athletic department in 2017, Texas was the only remaining NCAA Division I school to operate separate men's and women's athletic departments, after the other remaining holdout, the University of Tennessee, merged its men's and women's athletic departments at the end of the 2011–12 academic year. The University of Texas currently fields a varsity team in nine men's sports and 12 women's sports.

title: University of Texas at Austin - Wikipedia
content: # University of Texas at Austin. **The University of Texas at Austin** (**UT Austin**, **UT**, or **Texas**) is a public research university in Austin, Texas, United States. Founded in 1883, it is the flagship institution of the University of Texas System. With 53,864 students as of fall 2024, it is also the largest institution in the system. On March 6, 1967, the Sixtieth Texas Legislature changed the university's official name from "The University of Texas" to "The University of Texas at Austin" to reflect the growth of the University of Texas System. | Motto in English | "Education is the Guardian of the State" |. | Parent institution | University of Texas System |. The university is a major center for academic research, with research expenditures totaling $1.06 billion for the 2023 fiscal year. The university has also been affiliated with three Primetime Emmy Award winners, and as of 2021, its students and alumni have earned a total of 155 Olympic medals.

89K views · 1.4K reactions | In 1883, Texas made a promise.

The Texas Constitution had called for “a university of the first class.” Seven years later, on September 15, 1883, the University of Texas opened in Austin with 221 students and eight faculty members.

What people don’t realize is how small it was at the beginning.

There was no grand campus. No football stadium. No tower watching over Austin. Just one building on a limestone hill above the Colorado River, and an idea that Texas was ready to build something lasting.

And this is where it gets interesting.

That first campus sat on what became known as the Forty Acres, but in 1883, it was still a young institution in a young city, trying to become what the state had imagined on paper.

Over time, the hill changed. Buildings rose. Generations of students came through. Austin grew around it. And the university slowly became part of Texas identity itself.

Today, UT Austin reports 55,000 students, a long way from those first 221.  

But the detail that stands out most is this: the dream came before the campus.

Before the tower, before the crowds, before the Longhorns became known across the country, there was just a promise written into Texas history.

And in a way, that’s the most Texas part of the story.

Start with open land, a bold idea, and enough belief to build toward something nobody can fully see yet.

Did you know UT Austin started this small?
